summary.one_liner: AnyBar is a small macOS menubar app that shows a colored dot whose meaning and changes are controlled by UDP messages sent from scripts or other tools.
summary.what_it_does: AnyBar puts a single dot in the macOS menubar. It listens on UDP port 1738 by default, and sending a text command such as "red", "green", or "question" changes the dot's style. Built-in styles include white, red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, black, question, exclamation, filled, and hollow. Custom images placed in ~/.AnyBar can be shown by sending their name. The ANYBAR_PORT, ANYBAR_TITLE, and ANYBAR_INIT environment variables set the port, a text label, and the starting color, and several instances can run side by side. The README also lists client libraries and shell helpers for many languages, plus integrations such as build-status and command-monitoring tools.
use_cases: show build or CI status in the menubar
monitor long-running shell commands with a visual indicator
signal server or service health from scripts
run multiple status dots on different ports
display custom icons in the macOS menubar
how_to_run: Install with Homebrew Cask: brew install --cask anybar
Send a color command: echo -n "black" | nc -4u -w0 localhost 1738
Run multiple instances: ANYBAR_PORT=1739 open -na AnyBar
Quit by sending: echo -n "quit" | nc -4u -w0 localhost 1738
stack: Objective-C/Swift macOS app (inferred from AppleScript support and .app bundle)
notable: Controlled entirely by plain-text UDP messages, so any language or shell can drive it
Client libraries listed for Go, Node, Python, Rust, Ruby, Erlang, C#, Emacs, and more
AppleScript support for setting the dot and reading its state
Custom images from ~/.AnyBar at 19x19 or 38x38 pixels
filled and hollow styles adapt to menubar appearance changes on Big Sur
caveats: macOS only; the README describes OS X and Big Sur behavior
Client libraries and integrations are third-party and not maintained by the author
The README does not state a current maintenance status
